info.title: GamePedia Product 2.2 Play Intelligence API
info.description: Machine-readable contract for the Product 2.2 server surface: the canonical open game catalog, AI-assisted quick add, Playlog, Game DNA, Play Compass, Monthly Replay, the Today feed, the editorial magazine and the product control plane. This document covers only the /api/v1 Product 2.2 subset and is not the complete backend API; the deployed mobile gate subset stays in openapi/cross-platform.openapi.json, and every pre-existing unversioned route is unchanged by this contract. Trust model: a value a user supplied — a provider id, a title, a URL — is at most USER_CONFIRMED, and parsing the syntax of a store URL or a package id is not verification. Only a real server-side provider response or an editor decision produces a verified identity or a publicly visible catalog fact.

bearerAuth.description: Access token issued by POST /auth/login or POST /auth/refresh. Editor and admin capability is never read from this token: it is resolved from user_role_assignments on every privileged request.

CatalogProvenance.description: AI_INFERRED is never a source of truth and can never become a published fact without a human confirmation.

regionKey.description: GLOBAL when the provider key is not region scoped. (provider, externalId, regionKey) is unique in the database.

RegionalRelease.description: One country/language/platform service edition of a game work, with its own operator, availability window, server region and lifecycle status.

usableAsPublicHero.description: False for UNKNOWN, USER_SUBMITTED and RESTRICTED rights. An image that is not usable as a public hero must not be rendered as one.

input.description: Raw user input. It is used to resolve candidates and then discarded: only its SHA-256 fingerprint and the structured fields the user confirms are ever persisted. The server never fetches a submitted URL.

existingCandidates.description: At most three existing candidates, each with allowlisted match reason codes and a confidence.

matchReasonCodes.description: provider_identity_exact means a verified provider identity already exists. provider_identity_unverified means only an unverified row exists; parsing a store URL is not verification.

originalTitle.description: Null when no structured title could be derived. The raw natural-language input is never persisted as a fallback title.

requiresTitleConfirmation.description: When true, confirm must supply confirmedFields.originalTitle or the request is rejected with SUBMISSION_TITLE_REQUIRED.

aiFallbackUsed.description: True when AI failed, timed out, was over quota or returned a body that failed Zod validation, and the response degraded to a minimal manual draft.

publicReviewStatus.description: Public catalog visibility always requires review. AI never publishes and never merges.

selectedCatalogGameId.description: Link one of the previewed candidates instead of creating a new game. Mutually exclusive with confirmedFields.

requestPublicReview.description: Requests public listing. The submitter's own confirmation is never treated as review approval, and a submission can never produce a PUBLISHED catalog game: the information behind it is USER_CONFIRMED or AI_INFERRED at best. The parsed provider key is stored as an identity *claim*, never as a globally unique verified identity, so a submission cannot capture another account's future real provider sync.

note.description: Private user content. Never logged and never emitted as a Product Event property.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key. (userId, clientMutationId) is unique, so a retried create returns the original record instead of a duplicate.

deterministic.description: Game DNA is always computed deterministically. AI narration is optional and additive, and the endpoint works with AI disabled.

recommendations.description: At most three picks, drawn only from owned PLAYING/BACKLOG library entries. A default request never proposes an unowned game.

provenance.description: Read from the stored ownership provenance. PROVIDER_VERIFIED only when the server itself established ownership from a real provider response; a manual library write is USER_CONFIRMED; a row predating provenance tracking is UNKNOWN. Never inferred from gameSource.

ownershipVerified.description: True only when provenance is PROVIDER_VERIFIED.

action.description: Only these allowlisted actions can be recorded.

window.description: Half-open UTC window covering the local month. Boundaries are resolved through the timezone, so a DST transition inside the month cannot drop or duplicate an hour.

missingData.description: Structured explanation of anything the response could not account for.

status.description: A failing section is reported as unavailable while every other section still renders.

heroImage.description: Null unless the hero asset has a resolved rights status. An image with an unknown or restricted rights status is never offered as a public hero.

sources.description: Third-party references. Only the headline, a short excerpt, the source URL, timestamps and a content hash are stored; the full original text never is.

bodyFormat.description: Render with a CommonMark renderer that has HTML disabled. Raw HTML, script and data: URLs are rejected at write time, so a body never introduces markup or a remote resource of its own. Images come from the rights-reviewed article assets, not from inline Markdown.

bodyMarkdown.description: The body of the current revision. Non-null for a PUBLISHED or CORRECTED article; null for a reader when the article is not publicly readable. Third-party source text is never reproduced here.

revision.description: Metadata of the revision whose body is served.

changeNote.description: Required and non-empty for a CORRECTED revision.

featureFlagSource.description: 'database' means the kill-switch state was read successfully; a key with no row uses its configured environment default. 'database_unavailable' means the state could not be read at all, in which case every gated feature is reported and enforced as false.

features.description: Independent kill switches. Each feature can be disabled without affecting the others or any pre-existing endpoint.

featureFlagStateDegraded.description: True when featureFlagSource is database_unavailable. Product 2.2 endpoints then return 503 FEATURE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE. Pre-existing unversioned endpoints are unaffected.

eventId.description: Unique per event. A retried batch is idempotent and cannot double count.

properties.description: Allowlisted, shape-checked properties only. Raw queries, Playlog notes, URL query strings, provider bodies and prompts are dropped before the row is written.

Unauthorized.description: No valid bearer access token was supplied.

Forbidden.description: The account does not hold a required role. Editor and admin capability is resolved from the database, never from a JWT claim.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or belongs to another account and is therefore not disclosed.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

TooManyRequests.description: The shared per-user daily AI budget is exhausted.

FeatureDisabled.description: The feature's kill switch is off (FEATURE_DISABLED), or its state could not be read (FEATURE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE). Other features and every pre-existing endpoint keep working.

FeatureStateUnavailable.description: The kill-switch state could not be read, so the feature is enforced as disabled (FEATURE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE). Distinct from FEATURE_DISABLED, and retryable.

get.description: Deterministic ranking: score descending, then normalized title, then id. Only PUBLISHED games and the caller's own private registrations are visible.

200.description: Ranked catalog games.

get.description: A merged (tombstoned) id resolves to the surviving canonical game and reports resolvedFromMerge.

200.description: Canonical game detail with identities, localizations, regional releases, assets and per-field provenance.

post.description: Runs deterministic URL/app-id/package-id parsing, provider identity matching, locale alias and normalized title matching, then fuzzy ranking, and only reaches the LLM when those cannot answer. Nothing is written to the public catalog and nothing is merged.

200.description: Preview with up to three existing candidates and a new-game draft.

post.description: Writes only after explicit user confirmation. Creates a PRIVATE canonical game owned by the submitter, or links an existing candidate. requestPublicReview moves the submission to PENDING_REVIEW and never to PUBLISHED.

200.description: Existing candidate linked, or an idempotent replay of an earlier confirmation.

201.description: A new PRIVATE canonical game was created.

get.summary: Read one of the caller's own submissions
get.description: Another account's submission is reported as 404 rather than 403, so submission ids are not enumerable.

200.description: Submission state.

post.summary: Report corrections for a canonical game
post.description: A correction is recorded as field evidence with USER_CONFIRMED or OFFICIAL_SOURCE provenance. Nothing is published by this call, and the server never fetches the supplied source URL.

put.description: Idempotent: repeating the call updates the regional scope without creating a duplicate follow.

200.description: The caller now follows the game.
The caller no longer follows the game. Idempotent.

get.description: Keyset pagination on (playedAt desc, id desc), which is a unique total order, so a page can never skip or repeat a row.

200.description: The caller's own sessions only.
A retried clientMutationId returned the original record instead of creating a duplicate.

patch.summary: Update one of the caller's play sessions
patch.description: Ownership is part of the lookup, so another account's id resolves to 404.

200.description: The updated session, or an idempotent replay.

409.description: The clientMutationId was already used for a different play session (CLIENT_MUTATION_ID_REUSED). A reused key is a conflict, not a silent success.

delete.summary: Delete one of the caller's play sessions

200.description: Deleted, or an idempotent replay of an earlier delete.

409.description: The clientMutationId was already used for a different play session (CLIENT_MUTATION_ID_REUSED). A reused key is a conflict, not a silent success.

get.summary: Per-local-day play aggregates for one month
get.description: Day buckets are resolved in the supplied timezone. Note bodies are never returned.

200.description: Calendar aggregates.

get.description: Computed from ratings, library status, completion and drop outcomes, playtime, genres, Steam tags, recent play and Playlog outcome states. Playlog note bodies are never analysed.

200.description: Game DNA.

post.summary: Recommend at most three owned games to play now
post.description: Deterministic ranker with no model involvement. Candidates come only from owned PLAYING/BACKLOG library entries.

200.description: At most three recommendations with score components, reason codes, confidence, data freshness and ownership evidence.
Monthly replay, including an explicit empty-month state and structured notes for anything the response could not account for.

get.description: Sections are settled independently: one failing section is reported as unavailable while every other section still renders. Section order and in-section ordering are deterministic.

200.description: Today feed.

get.description: Only PUBLISHED and CORRECTED articles are readable. A hero image whose rights status is unresolved is withheld with a reason instead of being served.

200.description: Article.
Articles, newest update first with a deterministic slug tie-break.

post.description: Always created as DRAFT. An AI-assisted draft may only ever be DRAFT.

patch.summary: Update an article and advance its workflow state
patch.description: Update an article and advance its workflow state. Omitting bodyMarkdown keeps the existing body; an explicit null clears it. Transitions follow DRAFT -> FACT_CHECK -> RIGHTS_REVIEW -> SCHEDULED. PUBLISHED and RETRACTED are only reachable through their dedicated endpoints, which re-check the actor's role in the database. Changing content that is already public requires status CORRECTED with a non-empty changeNote, and sets correctedAt.

200.description: Updated article.

409.description: Either the transition is not allowed, or published content was changed without status CORRECTED (ARTICLE_CORRECTION_REQUIRED), or a correction omitted a non-empty changeNote (ARTICLE_CORRECTION_NOTE_REQUIRED).

post.description: Re-reads the actor's EDITOR/ADMIN role from user_role_assignments, and refuses when a hero image has an unresolved rights status.

200.description: Published.
Retracted.

get.summary: Versioned product configuration and kill-switch state
get.description: Intentionally not behind a feature flag: the client needs this response to learn which features are disabled.

200.description: Product configuration.

post.description: Event codes and property keys are both allowlisted, and every property is shape-checked. eventId gives idempotency. Intentionally not behind a feature flag so intake keeps working while a feature is disabled.

202.description: Batch accepted. Duplicates are reported rather than counted twice, and dropped property keys are echoed by name only.
